free_tier.stated: The host most often named in Chinese-language forums, quoted from its own front page: 20G KVM VPS with 20 GB RAID-10 SSD, 1 GiB RAM, 2 vCPU and 1 TB a month on a 1 Gbps port at USD 49.99 a year; 40G KVM at 2 GiB and 2 TB for USD 52.99 per half-year; 80G at 4 GiB and 3 TB for USD 19.99 a month; and a 320G shape at 16 GiB, 6 vCPU and 5 TB for USD 79.99 a month. Every plan allows datacenter migration, snapshots, rDNS and API access from its own KiwiVM panel.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: The datacenter-migration feature is worth more than the price: a box that can be moved between locations without reinstalling is the cheapest way to test which region a workload actually needs.

limits.value: One terabyte a month is the term that binds, and the plan is annual, so an overrun is corrected only at renewal. The plan is unmanaged: the vendor states self-managed KVM, so a broken image is the buyer's problem and there is no managed support tier at this price.

notes: New to the corpus: 805 compute records and no BandwagonHost record, although Chinese-language forums name it constantly and resellers price it in CNY. USD 49.99 a year is not the floor (DediOne at USD 3.99 a month and Tencent at CNY 99 a year are both cheaper), so this is recorded as the reference mid-price annual host with a migration feature, not as a bargain. The CN2 GIA plans that Chinese buyers actually pay for are on a separate store and were not read.
